name: Methimazole

fda.text: First Trimester Use of Methimazole and Congenital Malformations Methimazole crosses the placental membranes and can cause fetal harm when administered in the first trimester of pregnancy. summary: Taking Methimazole during the first three months of pregnancy can harm an unborn baby by crossing into the womb [3]. It has been linked to rare birth defects, such as missing skin patches, facial shape issues, and blocked nasal passages [3]. Based on a small computer model rather than tests on people, the drug received a medium risk score of 51 for the liver and a low risk score of 22 for the heart [M].
